top_authentic_signals.name: Sensor Noise Coherence
top_authentic_signals.summary: The frames share a consistent sensor-noise floor (1.42, 29% variation), consistent with a real camera.
top_authentic_signals.what_found: The frames share a consistent sensor-noise floor (1.42, 29% variation), consistent with a real camera.
top_authentic_signals.why_it_matters: A real camera leaves a steady noise floor in every frame. AI video generators rarely model true sensor noise, so it is often missing or flickers across frames, which is hard to fake.
top_authentic_signals.caveat: Heavy compression, denoising, and very detailed scenes affect this measurement, so it is weighed with the other signals.

top_ai_signals.name: Spectral Artifacts
top_ai_signals.summary: The Six-Lens model scored this image 95.8% AI / 4.2% authentic — a extremely high-confidence finding toward synthetic generation.
top_ai_signals.what_found: All six spectral lenses — visual texture (ConvNeXt), frequency grids (FFT), sensor noise simulation (SRM), color-space fingerprints (YCbCr), spatial reconstruction (SPAI), and robustness testing — collectively scored this image 95.8% AI. A score this strong, the majority of lenses independently flagged patterns like periodic frequency grids and noise distributions inconsistent with any known camera sensor profile.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: This model looks for patterns invisible to the human eye — buried in the pixel-level math of the image. A 95.8% score means the statistical fingerprint aligns significantly more with AI generation than camera physics, and these frequency-domain traces are very hard to remove without visibly degrading the image.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Heavy JPEG compression, aggressive resizing, or strong image filters can partially destroy the frequency-domain signals this model depends on, potentially softening a confident AI detection into an inconclusive result. Conversely, very new or unusual AI generators not present in training data may produce lower-than-expected scores.
